approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would extend the income management programme and its payment card for two more years while changing how it operates.
It would end certain incentive payments linked to income management, adjust the vulnerable measure, and tidy up the rules to help the programme work better.
It would also stop a residential care subsidy from 1 July 2015 for beds held empty for up to a week before a resident arrives, and would dissolve the aged care planning advisory bodies.
Extends income management and the BasicsCard for another two years.
Abolishes some incentive payments for income management.
Adjusts the vulnerable measure of income management.
Removes ambiguities to improve the programme's effectiveness.
Ends the holding payment for residential care places from 1 July 2015.
Repeals provisions for the Aged Care Planning Advisory Committees.
People on income management, residential aged care providers and care recipients, and the former advisory committees' functions.

The speaker opposed the bill's abolition of the 'vulnerable' income management measure and removal of Centrelink social worker support for at-risk recipients, but supported ending matched savings (up to $500) and voluntary incentive payments ($250). Labor argued for targeted income management requiring social worker assessments.

The bill extends income management for two years with $146.7 million, streamlines the system by removing social worker assessments, matched savings payments, and voluntary incentive payments, and amends aged care subsidies and abolishes Aged Care Planning Advisory Committees.

The speaker opposed the bill's cuts to social worker support for income management participants and aged care planning, citing projected savings of $11.6 million and the reduction of pre-entry leave for aged care, and criticized the government for removing the dementia and severe behaviour supplement.

The bill extends income management and the BasicsCard for two years, abolishes certain incentive payments, and from 1 July 2015 stops residential care subsidies for holding places before care entry. It also repeals redundant provisions for aged care planning advisory committees, which expired in September 2014.
